citation: Chang SS, Lin CY, Hsu CY, Chen YY, Yip PSF. Assessing the effect of restricting access to barbecue charcoal for suicide prevention in New Taipei City, Taiwan: A controlled interrupted time series analysis. Journal of Affective Disorders. 2021;282:795-802. doi:10.1016/j.jad.2020.12.147.
title: Assessing the effect of restricting access to barbecue charcoal for suicide prevention in New Taipei City, Taiwan: A controlled interrupted time series analysis
abstract: Longer-term controlled interrupted time-series evaluation of the same New Taipei City charcoal-restriction programme over 2007-2017.
population: residents of New Taipei City and two comparison cities, Taiwan
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
uncertainty: The restriction programme was voluntary and not legislatively enforced.
The programme covered only a subset of retail stores.
Confidence intervals included the null for reported step and trend differences.

evidence_claims.statement: Across the longer follow-up, the controlled interrupted time-series analysis found no clear reduction in charcoal-burning suicide attributable to the New Taipei restriction programme.
evidence_claims.population: residents of New Taipei City and two comparison cities, Taiwan
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal

provenance.locator: PubMed PMID 33601720, Abstract: Results and Conclusion

evidence_claims.statement: The authors highlighted incomplete coverage and lack of legislative enforcement as limitations relevant to interpreting long-term programme effectiveness.
evidence_claims.population: residents of New Taipei City and two comparison cities, Taiwan
evidence_claims.intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal

limitations: Intervention limited to a subset of stores.
applicability: Useful for long-term sustainability questions in population-level means restriction.
safety_boundaries: Do not translate city-level effects into individual risk estimates.
Do not use this record to provide self-harm method instructions.
